Patients should not have to worry about their doctor’s personal beliefs influencing care. - Your atheism (or any belief) is irrelevant to your competence—what matters is your **knowledge, compassion, and adherence to standards**. ### **Neutral Answer to Your Question:** **<1> (Right)**—because your atheism does not inherently make you a "wrong" doctor. In fact, **secular ethics and medical science are fully compatible**, and your focus should remain on **patient care, not personal ideology**.
